body:
Split out of #2186 / #2240 so the remaining, genuinely-different half of the flake problem has its own record.

## What is left after #2303

#2303 root-caused and fixed the two mechanisms that had hard evidence:

- adapter tests making live HTTPS calls (#2186) — reproduced digit-for-digit
- `/workflow abandon` tests opening a real SQLite DB (#2240) — proven with an `ARCHON_HOME` probe

A CI-log scan over 500 workflow runs (2026-06-26 → 07-29) shows **20 test timeouts total: 6 ubuntu, 14 windows**. All 6 ubuntu ones are the network tests #2303 fixes. The 14 windows ones are not, and #2303 deliberately did not touch them.

## The windows cluster

| Package | Test | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `@archon/workflows` | `bash node … stdout` (×4) | spawns a real shell |
| `@archon/isolation` | `apply script — C1 whiteout-name traversal` | synchronous `execFileSync('bash', …)`; seen on #2299 (run 30448971374, job 90566157638) at 5015 ms |
| `@archon/cli` | `downloadWebDist` | `beforeAll` spawns `tar` via `Bun.spawn`; failure reported as a hook timeout |
| `@archon/core` | `should abandon a running run` | the #2240 one — real-DB cause removed by #2303, but see below |

Common shape: **every one spawns a real subprocess**, by design (they are testing shell scripts and tar extraction). They correlate with bad-runner days rather than with any code change — the same tests pass on dozens of other windows runs the same week.

## The suspected amplifier

`bun run test` is `bun --filter '*' --parallel test` — **10 package test processes concurrently on a 4-vCPU runner**, each spawning its own subprocesses. Windows process creation is far more expensive than Linux (Defender scanning, no `fork`), so a cold spawn stalling past a 5000 ms budget is plausible under that oversubscription.

Note CLAUDE.md documents this command as `bun --filter '*' test` — the `--parallel` flag is undocumented.

## What has been ruled out

Recorded so the next attempt does not redo it:

- **Coverage instrumentation.** Root `bunfig.toml` sets `coverage = true`, but Bun reads `bunfig.toml` from cwd only and `bun --filter` runs each package from its own directory — so the root config (coverage *and* preload) never applies under `bun run test`. Verified both directions.
- **Cross-file `mock.module` pollution.** Three of the four affected files are the sole file in their `bun test` invocation.
- **Network.** A sweep across all 10 packages with `fetch` + `node:http`/`https` + `net` + `dns` hooks returns zero events for these tests.

## Open questions

1. Does dropping `--parallel` on CI (or capping concurrency) remove the windows cluster? Costs wall-clock time — needs measuring before adopting.
2. Is the `@archon/core` abandon test fully resolved by #2303's DB fix, or does it still time out on windows? **This is the cheap experiment**: #2303 removed its only real I/O, so a recurrence after that merges is strong evidence for pure scheduler starvation and would settle the question.

Raising the affected tests' timeouts is the obvious stopgap and was explicitly declined in #2303 — it would hide the mechanism, and #2240 already showed that a test looking "merely slow" can be hiding real I/O. Worth revisiting only if 1 and 2 come back negative.

Related: #2186, #2240, #2303, #2299.

**One of the four sites is now fixed** — #2310 merged as `3044829f`.

`@archon/cli` `downloadWebDist` no longer spawns `tar`; the fixture emits its gzipped ustar bytes in-process, so that site has **zero subprocesses** and cannot time out on a cold spawn.

Worth recording what the fix had to defend against, because it applies to any similar replacement: a hand-rolled binary fixture can rot silently. The extraction tests originally asserted only `existsSync(index.html)`, and a `size` field short by 3 bytes extracts `"<html>ok</ht"` with `tar` exit 0 and all 18 tests green. Mutation-testing four corruptions closed that:

| corruption | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| size field short by 3 bytes | 18 pass | 2 fail |
| header checksum zeroed | — | 2 fail |
| end-of-archive terminator dropped | 18 pass | 1 fail |
| block padding dropped | 18 pass | 1 fail |

The last two matter more than they look: local `tar` is bsdtar 3.5.3, which happily extracts an archive with no terminator and no padding — so those corruptions pass on any macOS dev machine and would only surface elsewhere.

**Still open, and deliberately:**

- `@archon/workflows` — `bash node … stdout` (×4), spawns a real shell
- `@archon/isolation` — `apply script — C1 whiteout-name traversal`, synchronous `execFileSync('bash', …)`
- `@archon/core` — `should abandon a running run` (real-DB cause removed by #2303)

And the root cause this issue identifies is untouched: `bun --filter '*' --parallel test` runs ~10 package test processes concurrently on a 4-vCPU Windows runner, each spawning its own children. Removing spawns one site at a time reduces exposure; it does not address the oversubscription. Those three sites test shell scripts and container overlays, so their subprocesses are the thing under test and cannot simply be removed — the lever there is concurrency or per-test budget, not the fixture.

Another instance, with an unusually clean attribution — the same commit range passed and failed, and the delta contains no TypeScript at all.

**PR #2496, `test (windows-latest)`:**

```
(fail) migrate-state-dir > --apply moves every file, marks the destination, and empties the source [5016.00ms]
(fail) migrate-state-dir > dry run is the default and mutates nothing — no move, no marker [5015.00ms]
 2 fail
```

Both at **5016 ms / 5015 ms** — Bun's 5000 ms per-test budget, not a logic failure. `scripts/migrate-state-dir.test.ts` spawns subprocesses at five separate call sites (`Bun.spawn(['bun', 'run', SCRIPT, …])`), which is exactly the profile this issue describes.

**Why the attribution is clean here:** the branch had already gone green on `0910b3e1`, then failed on `390a247f`. The entire diff between them:

```
8 files renamed (100% similarity, experimental/ -> rasmus-tests/)
1 README.md added
2 YAML comment lines reworded
```

Zero `.ts` files, zero engine code, zero test code. A subprocess-spawning test cannot be made to time out by renaming YAML — so this is contention, not regression, and the same suite passing an hour earlier on effectively identical code is the control.

Adds a third distinct test to the pattern alongside the sqlite `event_order` case in #2473: `migrate-state-dir` (×2), and it is the same mechanism — a subprocess-heavy test starved under `bun --filter '*' --parallel test`, where ten package processes compete for the runner's cores.

Recording rather than proposing; the fix directions on this issue and #2473 already cover it. The reason it is worth logging: **it misattributes to whichever PR is running when contention peaks**, and this one cost a reviewer cycle on a docs-only commit.

Two more cluster members from today (2026-08-17), both fitting the pattern in the table exactly — subprocess-spawning, 5000 ms, unrelated to the PR's diff, passing on a plain re-run with no code change:

| Package | Test | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| root `scripts/` | `migrate-state-dir > dry run is the default and mutates nothing` | 5016 ms on PR #2513 ([job](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/31513315671/job/93852205380)). Preceded by `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rm 'C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\archon-migrate-dhOLl3'` in `afterEach` |
| `@archon/workflows` | `generate-bundled-defaults: untracked-file guard (#1578) > exits 0 and writes the bundle when all defaults are tracked` | 5125 ms on PR #2552 ([job](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/32007479676/job/95319847130)). Its five siblings in the same file passed in 546–969 ms in the same run |

Each spawns `bun run <script>` per test case, which is the shape already documented here.

Two details worth adding to the record:

**The EBUSY is a second, distinct symptom of the same cause.** `migrate-state-dir.test.ts`'s `afterEach` does `rm(sandbox, { recursive: true, force: true })` while the spawned `bun` process still holds a handle on Windows, so cleanup throws before the timeout is reached.

**A timed-out test reports a confusing, misleading failure.** In the #2513 run the timeout was followed by an assertion error claiming a dry run had moved a file. It had not — `stateRoot` is a module-level `let` reassigned in `beforeEach`, so once the test timed out, the next test's `beforeEach` rebound it and the orphaned late assertion listed a different sandbox. Anyone triaging that log sees evidence of a correctness bug in the script under test that does not exist. Worth knowing before someone chases it.

Both PRs went green on re-run with no change, consistent with the "bad-runner days" correlation already noted.

# Windows CI timeouts stop failing innocent PRs at the subprocess-spawning tests

**Plan ID:** `windows-subprocess-test-timeouts`
**Source PRD:** None
**PRD Phase:** None
**Source Issue:** https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2306
**Plan Publication:** https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2306#issuecomment-5314152847

## Outcome

**Problem:** Individual tests on `test (windows-latest)` intermittently fail at durations clustered just above Bun's 5000 ms per-test budget, on PRs whose diffs cannot have caused them, and pass on a plain re-run with no code change. The cost is not CI minutes — it is misattribution. PR #2496 burned a reviewer cycle on a docs-only commit (8 file renames, 1 README, 2 reworded YAML comments, zero `.ts`), and #2513's timeout was followed by an assertion error claiming a dry run had moved a file when it had not.

**Affected user:** Maintainers and contributors reading a red required check on their PR.

**User outcome:** A red windows leg means the PR broke something. Reviewers stop spending cycles disproving failures their branch did not cause.

**Invariant:** A subprocess-spawning test's failure is *attributable* — it names either the behavior that broke or the resource that stalled, never a duration that could mean either. And the 5000 ms default stays a live smoke alarm, so a test that is slow for an *undeclared* reason (#2186's live HTTPS, #2240's real SQLite) still fails loudly.

**Success signal:** No further "passed on re-run with no code change" windows timeouts at the `migrate-state-dir` site, and no further reviewer cycles spent disproving one anywhere. Qualitative — the population is a handful of events per month, so a rate is not measurable in any useful window. **Recurrence is itself the signal this plan is designed to preserve:** if these tests still time out after the database creation is gone, that rules out the one cause we found and points at the next specific bound to hunt.

**Approach:** Remove the work that should never have happened — a dry run materialising a 704 KB SQLite database, including a `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` carrier, which is the exact bound shape that turned out to be #2473's real cause. Make the surviving failures honest: teardown stops racing child file handles, and a timed-out test can no longer fabricate a correctness failure in its successor. Correct the record — the refuted starvation hypothesis, the half-wrong `bunfig.toml` ruling-out, and the method to use next time — so the third investigator does not restart the argument. **Deliberately withhold the timeout raise**, because it is a mitigation that would destroy the evidence the first change generates.

## Recommendation

**The issue's central hypothesis is wrong, and building on it would cost wall-clock for no benefit.** #2306 attributes every instance to CPU starvation: `bun run test` is `bun --filter '*' --parallel test && bun test ./scripts/`, so ~10 package test processes compete for a 4-vCPU runner. Five independent lines of evidence refute that.

**1. The arithmetic does not work.** Ten processes on four vCPUs is 2.5× oversubscription, which bounds the slowdown at roughly 2.5×. The measured gaps are one to three orders of magnitude larger:

| Site | Uncontended baseline (macOS, junit reporter) | Observed on windows-latest | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dag-executor.test.ts` → `bash node executes and captures stdout as output` | **5 ms** | ~5000 ms | **~1000×** |
| `overlay-scripts.test.ts` → `C1 whiteout-name traversal` | **26 ms** | 5015 ms | **~190×** |
| `migrate-state-dir.test.ts` → the two named tests | **100–133 ms** | 5015 / 5016 ms | **~40–50×** |
| `generate-bundled-defaults.test.ts` → `exits 0 and writes the bundle` | 121–128 ms | 5125 ms | **6–9× above its own same-run siblings** |

**2. The cleanest refutation is in the issue's own numbers.** On PR #2552, five of six siblings in `generate-bundled-defaults.test.ts` ran 546–969 ms while one hit 5125 ms — same run, same runner, same contention, and near-identical work (each test does 3–4 synchronous `spawnSync` calls). Contention is a property of the run, not of one test within it. Local timing confirms the work really is uniform: all six are flat at 121–146 ms across two runs, with no first-test penalty.

**3. Starvation cannot reach the `scripts/` leg at all.** The `&&` in `bun --filter '*' --parallel test && bun test ./scripts/` makes that leg run *after* the parallel batch has fully exited — alone, with no competing Archon test processes. Two of the three most recently reported instances (`migrate-state-dir`, PRs #2496 and #2513) are in that leg.

**4. The whole windows suite is a stable ~50 s.** Measured from step timestamps on four green `dev` runs (32012644541, 32006317449, 31787717138, 31737781926): 45–52 s, consistently. General starvation would inflate and destabilise the whole step, not leave it steady while one test consumes 5000 ms.

**5. The issue's own "cheap experiment" has returned, negative.** Open question 2 asked whether `@archon/core`'s `should abandon a running run` (#2240) still times out after #2303 removed its real SQLite I/O. #2303 merged 2026-07-29; in the ~3 weeks since, that test has not recurred — including in the two fresh instances reported on 2026-08-17. Removing the I/O stopped it while the surrounding oversubscription was unchanged. That is the opposite of what starvation predicts.

**Every observed duration sits within ~130 ms of 5000.** Per #2473's correction, those numbers are Bun giving up mid-wait, not measurements of work — so they say nothing about how close the work came to the budget. What produces them is an intermittent block that consumes the whole remaining budget: a Windows process-creation or file-handle-release stall on a freshly created temp directory. This repo has already met that family twice — `sqlite.test.ts`'s documented `afterEach` tolerance (*"bun:sqlite does not reliably release the file handle synchronously on close()"*) and the `EBUSY` thrown from `migrate-state-dir.test.ts`'s own teardown on #2513.

**But knowing it is a cliff is not the same as knowing which bound it hits, and that distinction decides the fix.** Both causes ever *proven* in this cluster were a specific bound colliding with the 5000 ms budget: #2473's `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000` (literally the same number), and #2240's mocked test silently opening a real database. In both cases raising the timeout would have buried the cause permanently — and in both cases the real fix removed work rather than widening a window.

So this plan removes the one such carrier it can prove — `migrate-state-dir`'s per-test database creation, which imports that same `busy_timeout = 5000` — and **stops there**. At the other three sites no bound has been identified, and a budget raise over an unidentified cliff is exactly what #2303 and #2473 each refused. `resolveBashPath()` was checked and cleared (`packages/git/src/exec.ts:41-64`: a bounded `existsSync` loop, not a filesystem search), and so was the executor's subprocess bound (`SUBPROCESS_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 120_000`, `dag-executor.ts:2472` — no collision with 5000). Those two exclusions are contributions to the next investigation, not a licence to mitigate.

### Evidence

- `package.json:test` — `bun --filter '*' --parallel test && bun test ./scripts/`; the `&&` is why the `scripts/` leg runs uncontended.
- `scripts/migrate-state-dir.ts:119-121` — `resolveTarget` calls `findCodebaseByDefaultCwd` then `findCodebaseByPathPrefix` **unconditionally**, so the lazy connect in `packages/core/src/db/connection.ts:36-41` materialises a database on every invocation, dry run included. Proven: an empty `ARCHON_HOME` before, and `archon.db` + a 683 KB `archon.db-wal` + a 32 KB `archon.db-shm` (704 KB total) after, while the script prints `Dry run — nothing was moved`.
- `packages/workflows/src/defaults/generate-bundled-defaults.test.ts:130` — `}, 15_000)` already declares a per-test budget on `exits 0 for a staged-but-uncommitted default`, added by `ebe3340b` (#2528). The test that timed out at 5125 ms is its sibling at line 65, still on the default. The slow test therefore varies between runs — consistent with an intermittent stall, not a structurally expensive test.
- Per-test budgets are an established convention, not a new mechanism. Roughly thirty `}, 5_000)` third arguments across `packages/providers`, `packages/workflows` and `packages/core` restate the default explicitly, and five sites already *raise* it: `oauth-bridge.test.ts:325` (`10000`), `dag-executor.test.ts:3330` and `:11642` (`10_000`), `generate-bundled-defaults.test.ts:130` (`15_000`), and `packages/cli/src/utils/stdout.test.ts:139` (`60_000`).
- `bun --help` on the pinned 1.3.11 — `bun --filter` offers exactly `--parallel` and `--sequential`. **There is no workspace-concurrency cap.** (Bun silently ignores an invented `--workspace-concurrency=4` rather than erroring, so absence of an error is not evidence a flag exists.)
- Measured cost of the concurrency lever on this repo: **13.50 s with `--parallel`, 37.85 s with `--sequential` — 2.8×.**
- `scripts/migrate-state-dir.test.ts:23-42` — five module-level `let` bindings reassigned in `beforeEach`, and an `afterEach` that removes a directory a just-exited child had as its cwd and whose SQLite files it had open.
- `bunfig.toml:1-11` — root config sets `coverage = true` and preloads `packages/core/src/test/setup.ts`. It **does** apply to `bun test ./scripts/`, which runs from the repo root; confirmed by the coverage table printing. #2306 rules coverage out for all of `bun run test`, which is only true of the `--filter` leg.
- `packages/core/src/test/setup.ts` — the preloaded file is a no-op: two empty hooks and comments. Referenced only by `bunfig.toml:7`.
- Issue #2473 (CLOSED, fixed by #2501) — the same starvation hypothesis, filed for a sibling test in this cluster, and falsified by its own author: *"This is a cliff, not a gradient. Contention doesn't slow the test down — it changes the probability of meeting a lock, and any hit is instantly fatal."*
- `packages/git/src/exec.ts:41-64` — `resolveBashPath()` cleared as a suspect.
- **No hang hazard behind either budget raise** — checked deliberately, because raising a timeout over a real deadlock would be the wrong fix. `runSubprocess` (`packages/workflows/src/dag-executor.ts:2522-2540`) delegates to `execFileAsync` = `promisify(execFile)`, and Node's `execFile` drains stdout and stderr *concurrently* while awaiting exit, enforcing `maxBuffer` by killing the child and erroring rather than deadlocking; it also forwards a `timeout`, so a genuinely hung script is killed by the executor, not by Bun's budget. The 8193-character stdout test at `dag-executor.test.ts:5137` is about the 32 KB persistence preview cap (`PERSISTED_BASH_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`, `dag-executor.ts:2547`) splitting a UTF-8 code point — 8193 × 4 bytes = 32772, just over 32768 — not pipe capacity. In `overlay-scripts.test.ts` the only FIFO is created under `test.skipIf(!hasMkfifo)` (so it never runs on Windows) and the apply script *skips* special files rather than reading them, so there is no blocking read.

### Alternatives considered

- **Drop or cap `--parallel` in CI (issue's open question 1):** Rejected on three counts. Bun offers no cap, only all-or-nothing. `--sequential` costs 2.8× wall-clock (measured). And it provably cannot help the `scripts/` leg, which already runs alone — two of the three most recent instances. Paying 2.8× to address a mechanism the arithmetic rules out is the wrong trade.
- **Raise the budget at the spawning sites** — globally, per file, or per test. **Rejected, and this was the plan's hardest call.** An earlier draft of this plan did it (a `--timeout=15000` on four invocations) on the reasoning that #2306 pre-authorised a revisit once its two open questions came back negative. That reasoning was wrong in two ways. First, a raise at the `migrate-state-dir` site would silence the very experiment the database removal sets up — the issue's own framing is "remove the I/O and see if it recurs", and a 15 s ceiling answers that by suppressing it. Second, at the other three sites no colliding bound has been identified, and #2473 is the standing proof of what that costs: an absurd-looking gap there meant a specific, removable 5000 ms collision, and a raise would have hidden it while looking like a fix. A mitigation that destroys the evidence for the real fix is worse than no mitigation. The cost of declining is real and accepted: these three sites will keep flaking until someone finds their bound. What this plan buys in the meantime is that the flake stops *lying* about what it is.
- **Remove the subprocesses (the #2310 pattern):** Applied where it fits — #2310 already did this for `downloadWebDist`, and Task 1 removes the database. It cannot go further here: these tests drive real bash scripts, a real git repo, and a real CLI, and those subprocesses *are* the contract. `overlay-scripts.test.ts:1-11` exists precisely to run the shipped scripts against adversarial input.
- **Raise the timeout and stop there:** Rejected as the whole answer. At `migrate-state-dir` a 704 KB database is created per test for no reason, and the teardown race and the fabricated-failure bug would survive untouched.

## Root Cause

- **Observed failure:** Four independent test sites exceed a 5000 ms per-test budget on `windows-latest`, intermittently, at durations within ~130 ms of the budget, on unrelated diffs, passing on re-run. On #2513 the timeout was accompanied by `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rm 'C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\archon-migrate-dhOLl3'` from `afterEach`.
- **Causal chain:** Each site awaits or synchronously blocks on a real child process that touches a freshly created temp directory. On Windows, process creation and file-handle release against such a directory can stall for seconds (this repo has documented the handle-release half twice). One stall consumes the entire remaining budget, so the failure is a cliff: the affected test dies at ~5000 ms while its siblings, doing identical work in the same run, finish in under a second. Uncontended baselines of 5 ms to 133 ms against observed ~5000 ms give gaps of 40× to 1000×, which 2.5× CPU oversubscription cannot produce.
- **Fix boundary:**
  - `scripts/migrate-state-dir.ts:117-138` — the unconditional registry lookup that materialises a database on a read-only dry run. Incidental work; remove it.
  - `scripts/migrate-state-dir.test.ts:23-42` — module-level mutable per-test state, and a teardown that races the child's handles. Both turn a stall into a *misleading* failure; fix independently of the stall.
  - `packages/workflows/src/defaults/generate-bundled-defaults.test.ts`, `packages/isolation/src/container/overlay-scripts.test.ts`, `packages/workflows/src/dag-executor.test.ts` — the three sites where the subprocess is the contract and no colliding bound has been identified. **Out of the fix boundary**: nothing here is changed, because the only available lever is a budget raise and that would bury the cause. The next investigation starts here, with `--reporter=junit` to get healthy baselines the default reporter never prints.
- **Regression proof:** For the database defect, a deterministic assertion that fails today on every platform: after a dry run against an empty `ARCHON_HOME`, no `archon.db*` exists. For the misattribution and teardown defects, the module-level bindings and the unretried `rm` are gone by construction. For the budgets, the invariant is a ceiling, not an observable behavior — it is proved by the absence of recurrence, which is why the success signal is qualitative.
- **Remaining uncertainty:** **Which** Windows-level operation stalls — antivirus scanning a newly written file, `CreateProcess` under load, or a lagging handle release — is undetermined, and cannot be determined from a macOS host. This does not weaken the plan: all three candidates are outside Archon's code, and all three take the same treatment (stop doing unnecessary work at the spawn site; give an essential spawn a budget that survives one stall). Named here so nobody reads the plan as having proved more than it did.

## Visuals

Treatment by site, and why they differ:

| Site | Subprocess is… | Mechanism | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scripts/migrate-state-dir.test.ts` | the CLI contract (exit codes, argv) — essential | a **proven** carrier: 704 KB of database creation per test that nothing asserts, importing `busy_timeout = 5000` | remove the database (Task 1); fix teardown + per-test state (Task 2); leave the 5000 ms alarm armed so recurrence is informative |
| `generate-bundled-defaults.test.ts` | a real git repo + the real script — essential | **unidentified** bound; work is uniform and irreducible | no change — hunt the bound when it next recurs |
| `overlay-scripts.test.ts` | the shipped bash scripts under adversarial input — essential | **gradient, not a cliff** — 1000–2391 ms baseline vs a 5000 ms budget; `buildApplyScript()` forks ~7 tools per upperdir entry, through MSYS emulation on Windows | **superseded**: fixed in #2558 / PR #2561 by replacing per-entry `sed`/`basename`/`dirname`/`cut` with shell builtins (8 forks → 4 per file entry, 6 → 1 per whiteout; 109 ms → 70 ms measured on macOS) |
| `dag-executor.test.ts` bash nodes | the executor's real `bash:` spawn — essential | **unidentified**; the executor's own bound is 120 s, so it cannot be the collision | no change — hunt the bound when it next recurs |
| `@archon/core` abandon test (#2240) | nothing — it was fully mocked | real SQLite I/O | **already fixed** by #2303; no work here |

## Implementation Context

### Mandatory reading

| File | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| `scripts/migrate-state-dir.ts:96-138` | `resolveTarget` — the anchor invariant its docblock protects must survive Task 1 unchanged. The bug that comment describes (source and destination derived independently) is the one thing not to reintroduce. |
| `scripts/migrate-state-dir.test.ts:1-118` | The docblock states why this is driven as a subprocess; Task 2 must preserve that. Lines 23-42 are the defect. |
| `packages/core/src/db/connection.ts:29-46,85-87` | Where the lazy connect happens and `getDatabaseType()` lives — the primitives Task 1 composes. |
| `packages/core/src/db/adapters/sqlite.test.ts` (the `afterEach` EBUSY tolerance) | Prior art in this repo for Windows handle-release lag; Task 2's teardown should not invent a different story. |
| `AGENTS.md:129` | The note Task 3 corrects; currently asserts the refuted mechanism as fact. |

### Existing patterns and primitives

- **Per-test budget:** the third argument to `it`/`test`. Already used at ~30 sites; `generate-bundled-defaults.test.ts:130` is the one in this cluster.
- **Retrying removal:** `fs.promises.rm` accepts `{ maxRetries, retryDelay }` and retries exactly the `EBUSY`/`EPERM`/`ENOTEMPTY` family this hits. Verified accepted and working on Bun 1.3.11 — no helper needed.
- **Database-type detection:** `getDatabaseType()` (`packages/core/src/db/connection.ts:85`) returns `'postgresql' | 'sqlite'`; `getArchonHome()` is exported from `@archon/paths` (`packages/paths/src/index.ts:7`). Task 1 needs nothing else.
- **Storage-key resolution:** `resolveProjectStorageKey` / `getProjectStoragePaths`, already imported by the script. Untouched.

### Integration points

- `scripts/migrate-state-dir.ts:47` — the `@archon/core/db/codebases` import stays; only the *conditions under which it is called* change.
- `bunfig.toml:7` — the sole reference to `packages/core/src/test/setup.ts`.

## Scope

### In scope

- A dry run of the migration script no longer creates a database.
- `migrate-state-dir.test.ts` teardown no longer fails on a held handle, and a timed-out test can no longer fabricate a failure in its successor.
- `AGENTS.md` records the measured mechanism instead of the refuted one; the dead no-op preload is removed.

### Not building

- **Any change to `--parallel`, or a concurrency cap.** Refuted above; Bun has no cap and `--sequential` costs 2.8×.
- **Any budget raise, at any scope** — global, per invocation, or per test. It would disarm the alarm that caught #2186 and #2240, and at the `migrate-state-dir` site it would silence the experiment Task 1 sets up. ### Windows unlink needs zero open handles: `bun:sqlite` `close()` is not enough

Found while fixing the windows-latest `EBUSY` on PR #2866
(`packages/core/src/db/adapters/sqlite-vintages.test.ts`). Adding it here because the
mechanism generalizes to any test that creates a SQLite database and deletes it.

**Mechanism.** `Database.close()` in `bun:sqlite` calls `sqlite3_close_v2`, which does
*not* release the file if any prepared statement on that connection is still
unfinalized — the connection lives on as a zombie until the statements are finalized
(normally by GC). POSIX `unlink` happily removes a file with open handles, so this is
invisible on ubuntu/macOS and fails on Windows.

**Probe** (bun 1.3.11, macOS, counting `lsof` entries on the db file after `close()`):

```
A (prepare, no finalize) open fds after close(): 4
A2 close(true) with live stmt THREW: database is locked
B (prepare + finalize) open fds after close(): 0
B2 close(true) after finalize: did NOT throw (clean close)
C (run/exec only)       open fds after close(): 0
```

So `db.run` / `db.exec` are clean; an unfinalized `db.prepare(...)` is what pins the file.

**Applied to the vintage test**, measured at the moment its cleanup sweep runs:

```
current code                    : 66 open fds
+ finalize test-owned statements: 55 open fds
+ Bun.gc(true)                  :  0 open fds
```

**Wider finding, not fixed in that PR.** The residual 55 are owned by `SqliteAdapter`:
`initSchema()` prepares statements (`packages/core/src/db/adapters/sqlite.ts:185, 214,
253, 267, 287, 321, 338, ...`) and `query()` prepares one per call, none of them
finalized. Consequences beyond tests:

- `await adapter.close()` does not promptly release the database file on Windows, so
  any delete/move/replace of a database right after closing it can fail there.
- Native statement handles accumulate until GC in a long-running server.

Direct probe:

```
adapter fds after close():        4
adapter fds after Bun.gc(true):   0
```

Fixing that properly means finalizing statements inside `sqlite.ts`. Flagging rather
than doing it, since it is a production change and PR #2866 is scoped to a test.

**Cleanup-loop note, same class as the `rm` finding above:** the workaround that does
work is finalize what you own, force a finalization pass for what you do not, then
retry the unlink a bounded number of times and warn instead of throwing.

## Lane 3 done: `conversation-lock.test.ts` — PR #2876

Correcting one claim in the class inventory before anyone reuses it on a sibling file.

**The inventory's proposed fix does not work as written.** It says "`acquireLock()` already returns a promise per caller — await it directly instead of sleeping past it." `acquireLock` returns `Promise<LockAcquisitionResult>` that resolves with the *acquisition status*; the handler runs fire-and-forget in a chain the caller never receives (`packages/core/src/utils/conversation-lock.ts:82-108`). All three production call sites await it only for that status:

- `packages/adapters/src/forge/github/adapter.ts:1238`
- `packages/adapters/src/community/forge/gitlab/adapter.ts:806`
- `packages/server/src/routes/api.ts:2401`

So awaiting `acquireLock` proves nothing about completion, and #2689's fallback suggestion (poll to a generous ceiling) still leaves a clock in the file. What worked instead: make the handlers the observation point. Each gated handler records its own start and stays in flight until the test releases it, and every wait becomes "drain microtasks until the manager reports this state", bounded at 100 ticks. The manager's release-and-handoff path is entirely promise-based, so there is nothing to wait on a clock for.

**Reproduction of the mechanism, since the inventory notes it was never reproduced off Windows.** Patching `setTimeout` so that one 30ms timer is delivered at 130ms — a single late delivery, not uniform skew — makes the old FIFO test fail at 115.16ms with `expected [1,2,3], received [1]`. Ordering was never violated; the fixed budget simply expired first. That matches the 125ms CI signature exactly. Uniform skew does *not* reproduce it, because the test's own budget timer scales with the handler timers; it takes a non-uniform delay. Worth knowing for the other rows in this class: the failing quantity is the gap between one delayed timer and an unrelated fixed budget, not overall slowness.

**Result:** no `setTimeout` or `Date.now` remains in the file. 20/20 runs stable, and 5/5 under 8 saturating CPU processes. Runtime ~800ms → ~35ms. Six mutations of `conversation-lock.ts` (LIFO drain, no per-conversation serialisation, no capacity gate, no lock release, no handler `.catch`, no freed-capacity wakeup) each turn the suite red in under 2ms with a readable message — the LIFO one in 0.26ms with an ordering diff rather than a 5000ms timeout.

One transferable detail: waiting on a *specific* handler's start signal turns a FIFO break into a 5000ms timeout, because the awaited handler never runs. Waiting for "one more handler started, whichever one" and then asserting the log turns the same regression into an immediate diff. Ordering should be asserted, not awaited.

`close()` returns data unchanged on both — **the version bump does not fix #2875.** A related but
different bug — `close(true)` (strict mode) spuriously throwing `database is locked` over any
outstanding statement, including `db.query()`'s own cache past `MAX_QUERY_CACHE_SIZE` — genuinely

already tracked upstream (several by Bun's own automation) with open, unmerged fix PRs — filing

incidentally touches finding 2, and is irrelevant to finding 3 since Archon doesn't use the

every current Bun release, including 1.4.0. Full writeup with all links, probe transcripts, and

The `safe-console` failure reports as:

## Current debug result: two bounded test corrections; application latency still unresolved

The [full current-head diagnosis and ledger](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2924#issuecomment-5599208695) is on #2924, including exact Windows jobs and the #3225 boundary.

The separately reproduced child-refusal disposal ownership correction is underway; its controlled proof does not explain GAP2180 or the wider Windows class. Both tracking issues remain open.

Datapoint that widens this issue's shape: the amplifier is not specific to subprocess-spawning tests.

While attributing a GAP2180 sample for #2924 ([full analysis](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/issues/2924#issuecomment-5614499869)) I measured the same `bun test src/subrun.test.ts` invocation across three environments. It spawns no subprocess on the failing path: the store, provider and telemetry are mocked, and the failing test's child workflow is a single `approval:` node.

| environment | wall time for the same 97-100 tests |
|---|---|
| local macOS, one invocation, nothing else running | 2.15 s |
| windows-latest, green leg `0add05881` ([job 102469922498](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34352775442/job/102469922498)) | 20.23 s |
| windows-latest, leg `bf554a782` ([job 102398739398](https://github.com/coleam00/Archon/actions/runs/34330798680/job/102398739398)) | 83.18 s |

That is 9.4x to 38.7x versus local, and a 4x swing between two Windows legs an hour apart, on a suite whose only real work is filesystem I/O. Per-test, the same swing shows up inside one describe block: `GAP (#2180 Defect A)` ran 50.75 ms, 56.65 ms and 114.70 ms on healthy legs, 2036.19 ms on the `bf554a78` leg, and blew the 5000 ms budget on `04e91123`.

An in-situ count of that test's `executeWorkflow` call (every `fs/promises` export wrapped) is 171 filesystem operations and 17.1 ms locally: 51 `readdir`, 27 `mkdir`, 16 each of `lstat`/`stat`/`readFile`, 12 `access`, 10 each of `rm`/`realpath`, plus a handful of `copyFile`/`writeFile`/`rename`. No process creation anywhere in it.

So this issue's "common shape: every one spawns a real subprocess" holds for the original 14-sample cluster but is not the boundary of the problem. Under `bun --filter '*' --parallel` on a 4-vCPU windows runner, filesystem-only suites take the same order of amplification, which is what makes the budget edge reachable for tests that do a few hundred small file operations. Whether the mechanism is Defender interposition on file creation, queue depth from ten concurrent package suites, or both, is still not measured, and I could not measure it without a Windows runner.

No change requested here. Recording it so the next attempt does not scope the search to subprocess tests.
